title: OpenAI-Upwork Study: AI Freelance Briefs 45% More Diverse
summary: OpenAI and Upwork report finds AI-related freelance projects grew 45% more diverse in task mix between January 2025 and June 2026, with larger budgets.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- AI-related freelance briefs on Upwork grew 45% more diverse in task mix, rising from 14.6 to 21.2 equally common tasks between early 2025 and mid-2026.
- These projects carry 52% higher fixed-price budgets and 41% more hours in the first 90 days, but posted hourly rates remain nearly flat at just 1.5% higher.
- Across 63 work categories, 43 saw ChatGPT-common tasks lose share on Upwork, suggesting AI recombines work rather than simply replacing jobs.


A joint study from OpenAI's Economic Research Team and Upwork, officially released on November 10, 2026, reveals that AI-related freelance project briefs have grown 45% more diverse in their task mix over the past 18 months. The shift, measured between January 2025 and June 2026, saw the number of equally common tasks per AI-related posting climb from approximately 14.6 to 21.2. The report, titled 'Work at the Frontier: AI's effect on freelance work,' offers the most detailed look yet at how generative AI tools are reshaping the structure and economics of online contract work.


## Task Diversity Surge in AI Projects


The 45% increase in task diversity signals a fundamental change in how clients scope AI-enabled work. Rather than posting narrow, single-skill requests, employers are now bundling a wider array of activities into individual briefs. The study quantifies this using an entropy-based measure that captures how evenly distributed different task types are within a posting. A higher number indicates more variety. By late 2025, AI-related postings had reached 21.2 equally common tasks, compared to 14.6 in early 2023. One example cited in the report: a single brief requesting "AI-generated video, editing and motion graphics in a single delivery."


## Budget and Hours Rise, Hourly Rates Stay Flat


Despite the broader scope, posted hourly rates for AI-related work increased by only 1.5% relative to the rest of Upwork's marketplace. The real economic shift appears in project scale. Fixed-price budgets attached to AI briefs run approximately 52.4% higher than non-AI postings, and hours logged in the first 90 days are about 40.6% greater. The report emphasizes that the finding reflects more work attached to each project rather than a demonstrated hourly pay premium. Freelancers taking on AI-related contracts are handling larger, more complex engagements without a proportional increase in their per-hour compensation.


## ChatGPT Use and Work Category Shifts


To understand where AI tools are reconfiguring demand, the study matched ChatGPT usage data from January 2025 to June 2026 against Upwork posting patterns across 63 freelance work categories. In 43 of those categories, tasks that are relatively common inside ChatGPT lost share on Upwork. In 20 categories, the opposite occurred. Writing, for instance, shows up more heavily in ChatGPT activity than in Upwork postings, while video and animation remain more prominent on the freelance platform. The pattern suggests recombination: AI tools handle certain tasks directly, freeing clients to post briefs that emphasize skills less easily automated or that require human oversight.


## Release Date and Context


The report was officially released on November 10, 2026, the same day Anthropic announced that its Fable 5.2 model cleared 41% of real Upwork projects in a separate benchmark. The OpenAI-Upwork analysis does not isolate how much of the observed pattern is attributable to ChatGPT versus other AI tools, noting only that the trends align with periods of rapid generative AI adoption. The study draws on Upwork's internal posting metadata and OpenAI's anonymized usage logs, applying econometric techniques to control for seasonal and category-level variation.


## What This Means


The 45% jump in task diversity points to a labor market where AI acts as a catalyst for bundling rather than outright displacement. Clients are assembling more multifaceted projects, and freelancers must navigate a wider skill set per engagement. While hourly rates have not surged, the shift toward larger budgets and longer timelines could create new opportunities for workers who can integrate AI tools into hybrid workflows. For platforms and policymakers, the finding underscores the need to track task recombination alongside traditional job-loss metrics, as the real transformation may lie in how work is packaged rather than how many jobs disappear.
